transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-26 14:00 UTC, Duration ~46 minutes. Attendees listed in metadata.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, this is Alex from Redwood, im joined by Samira our systems eng, and Jordan from CSM. quick check—audio ok?
[00:10] Maya (Silverline InfoSec): yes loud and clear, thanks.
[00:15] Alex: cool, so objective today is to walk through audit logs and admin activity logging — what we capture, export options, retention, encryption/KMS, and answer any compliance questions. feel free to interrupt.
[00:28] Tom (Eng): quick background — Silverline uses an in-house SIEM (we run Splunk), retention policies are strict for payments data, and legal requires 7 years of admin activity for audits. we also have a key mgmt requirement, customer-managed KMS is preferred.
[00:43] Samira (Redwood SE): great — we'll cover what fields we log, where logs live, export paths (S3/HTTP/Syslog), retention controls, and KMS integration. I'll start with the log schema then hand to Alex for compliance bits.
[00:58] [Samira] so first, audit events: we capture admin logins, role/permission changes, token/credential creation, model-version rollouts, config changes (route/policy updates), and data export events. timestamps, user_id, ip, region, request_path, outcome (success/failure), and a free-form message. note: some product-specific names may appear slightly off in export — like "redwood-route" sometimes shows as "r-route" in older agents, that was a transcription quirk, sorry.
[01:30] Maya: when you say token creation — do you log the token value? we need to be sure PII/secret values are never persisted.
[01:36] Samira: correct, we never persist raw secrets. we log the event and a token id/nonce, but not the secret. tokens are hashed at rest for lookup only.
[01:44] Priya (Cloud Infra): you mentioned region — is region inferred from request headers or from route? we have data residency constraints in eu-west only.
[01:52] Samira: region is inferred from the serving region that handled the request. for hosted customers you can pin region; for private we run in your VPC so residency is controlled by deployment.
[02:05] Evan (Compliance): retention — what's default and can we override per-account? legal typically wants immutable logs kept separate.
[02:12] Alex: default retention for audit logs on hosted plan is 90 days for quick access, with archived export options to S3 for long-term retention. for enterprise we offer configurable retention windows and can push exports automatically to a customer-managed S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.
[02:27] Maya: and are archived logs tamper-evident? chain of custody?
[02:31] Samira: when exporting to S3 you can enable server-side encryption with your KMS key, and we optionally sign exports with an export manifest. for extra tamper-evidence we can enable immutable S3 object lock (governance/compliance mode) if you provide the bucket and permissions.
[02:48] Tom: can we stream logs to Splunk in near-realtime? we need <1 min latency for critical admin events.
[02:55] Samira: yes — we support a webhook streaming endpoint and native syslog over TLS. throughput and batching are tunable; critical events can be pushed immediately while others are batched. the webhook includes a seq id and timestamp. we've seen sub-30s delivery for critical paths in other deployments but network variability applies.
[03:17] Maya: curious about the schema — do you include request/response payloads or only metadata?
[03:22] Samira: by default we log metadata and identifiers; request payloads are not included unless the customer explicitly enables a debug-level capture for a scoped timeframe. enabling payload capture is a controlled opt-in and defaults to masking PII. we recommend using it only for troubleshooting.
[03:40] Evan: for audits we need admin activity reports — is there a UI or do you provide CSV exports?
[03:46] Alex: both — the console has pre-built audit reports and filters for admin activity; you can export to CSV/JSON. we also provide an API to pull logs programmatically. Samira will share a sample CSV schema after the call.
[04:01] [Samira] note — the CSV columns include event_time, user_email, user_id, action, resource, outcome, ip_address, region, request_id, session_id, and message. sample file sometimes shows odd capitalization from transcribers — like s-Id vs sessionId — but schema is consistent.
[04:22] Tom: talk to me about access controls for viewing logs — RBAC, SSO integration etc. we need separation of duties.
[04:29] Samira: RBAC is granular — you can grant view-only audit roles, admin roles, or config roles. We integrate with SAML/SSO (Okta, Azure AD), mapping SAML groups to Redwood roles. all actions in the console are logged as admin events.
[04:46] Maya: do you support attribute-based access? e.g., restrict log visibility by region or business unit?
[04:52] Samira: we have role scoping for org<-project levels; advanced attribute-based rules are on the roadmap but not GA. for now you can partition using projects and route logs by project/region.
[05:06] Evan: encryption at rest — you mentioned KMS. do you support customer-managed keys across both logs and models?
[05:13] Alex: yes — customers on enterprise/private can use CMK (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). logs stored in our managed store can be encrypted using a CMK or our managed keys; for S3 exports you can require the objects be encrypted with your key.
[05:26] Priya: and key rotation — what's the process? we have strict rotation policies.
[05:30] Samira: we support key rotation for CMKs. we recommend rotating keys and configuring the external S3 lifecycle to re-encrypt if needed. we maintain backward-compatible decryption for a rotation window; details are in the security whitepaper.
[05:45] Tom: audit integrity — do you provide hashes or signed manifests for exported batches?
[05:50] Samira: yes we can provide a signed manifest per export batch containing checksums (sha256) for each object and a manifest signature. that helps with chain-of-custody verification.
[06:02] Maya: what about admin impersonation — is there a way to see if the action was performed by an automated service account vs a human?
[06:09] Samira: events include actor_type (user, service, api-key), and we log both the originating principal and any assumed role. there is also session_id and user_agent.
[06:20] Alex: i'll add that platform-level service actions are tagged and separated from customer-initiated actions in the audit index.
[06:28] Evan: are logs single-tenant or sharded? concern about co-mingling.
[06:33] Samira: logs are tenant-scoped. on hosted we logically separate indexes per customer. for Dedicated/Private deployments you have physical separation.
[06:43] Maya: regulatory question — do you provide time-synchronized timestamps (ntp) and timezone normalization? the auditors ask for consistent times.
[06:51] Samira: all events have UTC timestamps from a synchronized time source and we include both received_time and event_time fields. timezone normalization for the console is available in the UI.
[07:04] Tom: SIEM mapping — do you map fields to common schemas like CEF or ECS?
[07:09] Samira: we provide an ECS-compatible mapping and also CEF for Splunk customers. the export includes both raw and mapped fields.
[07:20] Maya: what about retention enforcement — can a normal admin delete logs or do deletions require elevated processes?
[07:27] Samira: deletion of logs is restricted — only designated compliance roles can request deletions and deletions are themselves logged with an approval workflow. for archival exports we recommend immutability on the target bucket.
[07:42] Alex: circling back — for Silverline specifically, we recommend using a customer-managed S3 bucket with object lock enabled, CMK encryption, and webhook to your Splunk for realtime alerts. we'll also set the audit retention in-redwood to 90 days for quick retrieval and run nightly exports.
[07:58] Priya: can the nightly exports be incremental? we prefer delta exports for bandwidth.
[08:03] Samira: yes — we support incremental exports with watermarking by event_time. the manifest will include the watermark for resumable pulls.
[08:15] Maya: demo time? can we see the console audit view and export UI?
[08:19] Alex: quick share — im pulling up the audit logs page now.
[08:24] [screen share sounds, slight delay]
[08:30] Samira: here's the filters — event type dropdown, outcome, user, region. clicking export opens options: CSV to local, scheduled S3 push, or webhook. you can choose encryption method and attach manifest signing.
[08:46] Tom: i see sample export options here. in the CSV i noticed a column called request_id and sessionId, are both guaranteed?
[08:53] Samira: request_id is generated for every API call; sessionId exists for console sessions and can be null for API-only actions. we include both when present.
[09:05] Maya: small nit — our auditors want obfuscation of IPs after 30 days. is that supported?
[09:12] Samira: we have a configurable PII mask policy — you can redact or hash IPs after a configurable window, or keep raw IPs in the archived export. masking is applied at export time.
[09:25] Evan: curious about legal holds — if we need to preserve a set of logs beyond retention, can we place a hold?
[09:31] Alex: yes — we support retention holds per project/account. holds prevent lifecycle deletion and are logged as well.
[09:39] Priya: performance impact — does audit logging add latency to API calls?
[09:44] Samira: negligible for metadata events — logging is async and writes to a durable write-ahead log. we only synchronously block when debug payload capture is enabled.
[09:55] Tom: Do you support exporting to on-prem SIEM via a private link? we have an air-gapped ingestion node.
[10:01] Samira: for Private/Dedicated deployments we can configure a direct peering or private link to push logs; for hosted we can push to a customer-managed VPC endpoint if you provide network connectivity.
[10:14] Maya: any caveats for FedRAMP or PCI?
[10:18] Alex: we're not FedRAMP certified yet. for PCI, we have controls and audits in place, and many payments customers run Dedicated or Private to satisfy PCI network segregation. we'll share our compliance pack.
[10:31] Evan: what about retention account billing — does long-term archived logs cost extra?
[10:35] Alex: archived exports to customer S3 incur egress/export operational fees plus storage on your side. Redwood can also store archives for a fee under enterprise terms. We'll include numbers in the quote.
[10:48] Priya: would love to see the sample CSV and webhook payload now, or after the call?
[10:53] Samira: I'll send them after the call. here's a quick spoken example: {event_time: "2026-03-26T13:58:23Z", user_email: "m.ortiz@silverline.com", action: "grant-role", resource: "project-7", outcome: "success", request_id: "r-abc-123"} — note that's illustrative.
[11:15] Maya: sounds good. one more compliance question — can you attest that logs are immutable for the period? we need an SLA statement.
[11:23] Jordan (CSM): we can include immutability and retention commitments in a contract addendum for enterprise deals. i'll coordinate legal language and share a draft.
[11:33] Evan: outstanding — how do we validate integrity during audits? is there an API to fetch manifest signatures?
[11:39] Samira: yes — manifest and signature are available via the exports API and we can provide verification tooling or a script to validate sha256 checksums against objects.
[11:52] Tom: any gotchas if we onboard during a production cutover? we may want a 2-week parallel run.
[11:58] Alex: common approach is a 2-week ingest parallel run — you route copies to our staging ingest and to your SIEM to validate schema and latency. we'll support that and provide runbooks.
[12:12] Maya: ok recap for me: we want nightly incremental exports to our S3 with object lock, CMK encryption, webhook to Splunk for realtime alerts, retention hold ability, and RBAC mapping from Okta. is that accurate?
[12:25] Alex: yup exact. we'll also provide a sample CSV, SOC2, signed manifests, and schedule a PoC with Priya.
[12:33] Priya: timeframe — can we kick off PoC next week?
[12:36] Alex: yes we'll aim for the week starting 2026-04-06. Samira, Jordan can you both coordinate?
[12:42] Samira: yes.
[12:44] Jordan: yep i'll send calendar invites.
[12:47] Evan: any final items we should flag?
[12:50] Maya: just please include the legal wording for immutability and retention holds, and the CMK rotation support note.
[12:58] Alex: will do. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and sample exports.
[13:04] [call ends]

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; speaker labels may slightly differ from calendar. Attached references mentioned: security whitepaper (link shared via email), SOC 2 Type II report (link), export-sample.csv (to be sent).
